children: Brent crude falls below $100 a barrel on hopes for a diplomatic push to end the U.S.-Iran war. The global oil benchmark is down 1.2% to $99.11 a barrel, while the U.S. oil gauge WTI is down 2.7% to $93.20 a barrel after Japan's Kyodo News reported that Iran has proposed to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the American blockade is lifted. "The report triggered fresh selling, as traders read it as a fresh de-escalation signal ahead of this week's U.N. General Assembly," says Kaynat Chainwala from Kotak Securities. "Until a concrete outcome emerges from this week's meetings, crude's risk premium looks vulnerable to further unwinding, though stalled talks could just as quickly reverse the move." (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)
